findings.description: SYS-SUP-022 requires the outputs and status signal to reach their specified levels within 50 ms of the detectable instant. OP-SWR-001 states that the software budget consumes the full 50 ms up to the output write while assuming negligible output-drive delay; the inputs do not establish that delay. The allocation therefore does not establish that the system deadline can be met.
findings.requested_change: classify OP-SWR-001 as blocking

findings.description: SYS-SUP-020 requires the outputs and status signal to remain low from any reset, but the requirement and its rationale cover only the period from the start of software start-up. OP-SWR-002 identifies an unspecified hardware-controlled interval before the first software action, so the allocated behavior cannot be established from the inputs.
findings.requested_change: classify OP-SWR-002 as blocking

findings.description: The requirement calls for the last eight fault reports even when fewer than eight exist. OP-SWR-004 leaves the response for that condition undecided, so a verifier cannot determine the required result immediately after a power-on reset or before eight reports have been recorded.
findings.requested_change: classify OP-SWR-004 as blocking

findings.description: The timestamp is defined as milliseconds since the latest reset, but neither SWR-RPT-005 nor CON-SUP-126 identifies the instant to timestamp. Detection and transmission can occur at different times under SWR-RPT-001, producing different valid interpretations.
findings.requested_change: Obtain or reference a decision identifying the event whose elapsed time is reported, and specify it in the requirement.

findings.description: The requirement does not identify the event whose time is reported. CON-SUP-126 defines the reset reference and number format, but detection and transmission can occur at different times, so the expected timestamp cannot be determined uniquely.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-SWR-006 and specify the event whose elapsed time is reported.

SWR-OUT-003 allocates the full 50 ms to the software output write, while OP-SWR-001 assumes an unspecified output-drive delay is negligible. The allocation therefore does not establish that the system deadline can be met.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SWR-001 as blocking and establish a supported software and hardware timing allocation.

findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SWR-004 as blocking.

findings.requested_change: Obtain the decision recorded in OP-SWR-006 and specify the event whose elapsed time is reported.

findings.description: SWR-DIA-003 requires retrieval of the last eight fault reports and SWR-SAF-004 requires retained fault history, but the set does not require reports to be added to that history. Retaining an unchanged history would satisfy SWR-SAF-004 without providing the reports required by SYS-SUP-034.
findings.requested_change: Specify how fault reports enter the retained history so the last available reports can be retrieved.

findings.description: SWR-SAF-002 requires recognition of three consecutive detections of the same code without 60 seconds of fault-free operation, including detections across resets. SWR-SAF-004 retains the latch, history and fault count but the set does not specify preservation of the consecutive-detection and elapsed fault-free information needed to apply that rule across resets.
findings.requested_change: Specify the retained information and reset handling needed to evaluate the repeated-fault rule across software and watchdog resets.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-022 requires the physical outputs and status signal to reach their specified levels within 50 ms of the detectable instant. SWR-OUT-003 allocates the full 50 ms to the software output write, while OP-SWR-001 assumes an unspecified output-drive delay is negligible. The allocation does not establish that the system deadline can be met.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SWR-001 as blocking and establish a software timing allocation that accounts for the output-drive delay.

findings.description: The requirement calls for the last eight fault reports even when fewer than eight exist. OP-SWR-004 leaves the response for that condition undecided, so the expected result cannot be determined after power-on or before eight reports have been recorded.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SWR-004 as blocking and define the response when fewer than eight reports exist.

findings.description: The requirement does not identify the event whose time is reported. CON-SUP-126 defines the reset reference and number format, but detection and transmission can occur at different times, so the expected timestamp cannot be determined uniquely.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-SWR-006 and specify the event whose elapsed time is reported.

findings.description: SWR-SAF-007 retains elapsed fault-free operation time, but SWR-SAF-009 requires updating the retained values only at fault detection. The set does not require elapsed time to advance during fault-free operation. Its rationale also resets the time at each detection, although SWR-SAF-002 refers to time since the first detection. These gaps prevent reliable application of the repeated-fault rule across resets.
findings.requested_change: Specify how fault-free operation time is updated and how the 60-second condition is evaluated across detections and resets, consistently with SYS-SUP-028.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-022 requires the physical outputs and status signal to reach their specified levels within 50 ms of the detectable instant. SWR-OUT-003 allocates the full 50 ms to the software output write, while OP-SWR-001 assumes an unspecified output-drive delay is negligible. The allocation does not establish that the system deadline can be met.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SWR-001 as blocking and establish a software timing allocation that leaves a justified share for output-drive delay.

findings.description: SWR-DIA-003 calls for the last eight fault reports even when fewer than eight exist. OP-SWR-004 leaves the response for that condition undecided, so the expected result cannot be determined after power-on or before eight reports have been recorded.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SWR-004 as blocking.

findings.description: SWR-RPT-005 does not identify the event whose time is reported. CON-SUP-126 defines the reset reference and number format, but detection and transmission can occur at different times, so the expected timestamp cannot be determined uniquely.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-SWR-006 and identify the event whose time is reported.

findings.description: SWR-SAF-011 advances the retained elapsed time at every control cycle while a sequence exists, including cycles after a fault has been detected. SYS-SUP-028 requires 60 seconds of fault-free operation. Counting fault-handling time can cause a repeated-fault sequence to expire before 60 seconds of fault-free operation have elapsed.
findings.requested_change: Specify when fault-free operation time advances and preserve that meaning across detection, fault handling and reset.

findings.description: CON-SUP-004 requires C11 as well as prohibiting dynamic allocation and recursion. SWR-RES-002 covers the latter two constraints, but the software requirements do not address the C11 language constraint.
findings.requested_change: Address the C11 language constraint in the software requirements or record its disposition.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-020 requires both control outputs and the status signal to remain low from any reset. SWR-OUT-001 covers only the period from the start of software start-up; OP-SWR-002 leaves the preceding hardware-controlled interval unspecified.
findings.requested_change: classify OP-SWR-002 as blocking

findings.description: SYS-SUP-022 requires the physical outputs and status signal to reach the specified levels within 50 ms of the detectable instant. SWR-OUT-003 allocates the full 50 ms to the software output write, while OP-SWR-001 assumes an unspecified output-drive delay is negligible.
findings.requested_change: classify OP-SWR-001 as blocking

findings.description: SWR-DIA-003 calls for the last eight fault reports even when fewer than eight exist. OP-SWR-004 leaves the response for that condition undecided, so the expected result cannot be determined after power-on or before eight reports have been recorded.
findings.requested_change: classify OP-SWR-004 as blocking

findings.description: SWR-RPT-005 does not identify the event whose time is reported. CON-SUP-126 defines the reset reference and number format, but detection and transmission can occur at different times, so the expected timestamp cannot be determined uniquely.
findings.requested_change: Obtain the event to timestamp through OP-SWR-006 and specify it in the requirement.

findings.description: SWR-SAF-011 adds a full 10 ms at the end of a control cycle whenever start-up checks have passed in that cycle, even if they passed partway through it. Across resets this can count time before fault-free operation began and expire the sequence before the 60 seconds required by SYS-SUP-028.
findings.requested_change: Define how elapsed fault-free operation is measured across partial start-up cycles so that the sequence cannot expire before 60 seconds of fault-free operation.

findings.description: OP-SWR-007 says the inputs do not decide whether reset time counts toward the 60 seconds in SYS-SUP-028, but SWR-SAF-007 and SWR-SAF-011 exclude that time. If reset time counts, the retained elapsed time and resulting latch decision can disagree with the system requirement.
findings.requested_change: classify OP-SWR-007 as blocking

findings.description: SYS-SUP-028 and CON-SUP-135 count elapsed time in the OPERATIONAL state. Adding 10 ms based only on conditions at a cycle's end can count time before start-up checks passed; discarding a cycle when a fault occurs can omit time spent operational before detection. Across resets, these errors can change whether the 60 s threshold has been reached and therefore whether SWR-SAF-002 latches.
findings.requested_change: Specify elapsed-time accounting that counts only time actually spent in the OPERATIONAL state, including partial cycles across state transitions and resets, with sufficient precision to decide the 60 s latch condition.

findings.description: OP-SWR-008 acknowledges that a watchdog reset can discard operational time since the last update. This can cause a latch after 60 s of fault-free operation, contrary to SYS-SUP-028. Acceptability of that deviation requires a decision at this stage, so deferring it to software architecture hides a decision needed for a correct requirement.
findings.requested_change: classify OP-SWR-008 as blocking

findings.description: The requirement specifies 100 µs resolution and its rationale accepts unresolved fractions for the 60 s decision. CON-SUP-103 specifies that resolution for task start and execution measurements; it does not authorize rounding or loss of elapsed operational time for the threshold in SYS-SUP-028. Quantization can change the latch decision near 60 s.
findings.requested_change: Remove the unsupported acceptance of quantization error or record a blocking open point for an authorized timing tolerance and apply the resulting decision to the requirement.

findings.description: SWR-SAF-011 requires exactly the time spent in OPERATIONAL, but its rationale and OP-SWR-008 acknowledge that a watchdog reset can lose operational time since the last addition. This can change the 60 s decision required by SYS-SUP-028; the inputs do not authorize that loss.
findings.requested_change: classify OP-SWR-008 as blocking

findings.description: SWR-SAF-011 requires exact elapsed time measured at 100 µs resolution, without an allowable measurement or accumulation error. CON-SUP-103 specifies that resolution for task timing, not exact operational-time measurement. OP-SWR-009 identifies the missing tolerance needed to verify the 60 s decision.
findings.requested_change: Obtain the permitted elapsed-time tolerance and update the requirement and its verification criteria accordingly.

findings.description: SWR-SAF-011 requires all time spent in OPERATIONAL to be accumulated, but OP-SWR-008 states that an unannounced watchdog reset can lose time since the last addition. That loss can change the 60 s latch decision required by SYS-SUP-028.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SWR-008 as blocking and resolve the permitted treatment of operational time lost on an unannounced reset.

findings.description: SWR-SAF-011 requires exact accumulation of operational time measured at 100 µs resolution without an allowable measurement or accumulation error. CON-SUP-103 specifies that resolution for task timing, and OP-SWR-009 identifies the missing tolerance for the 60 s decision.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-SWR-009 and specify a measurable operational-time accuracy consistent with the resulting decision.
